links.outcome: Readability and semantic fidelity of LLM-simplified health texts across general-purpose and domain-adapted models
links.effect: General-purpose LLMs reduced sentence complexity and improved fluency but occasionally introduced semantic shifts or omitted critical health information; domain-adapted models were more faithful but less readable due to retained jargon.
links.quote: Our findings reveal that while general-purpose LLMs excel at reducing sentence complexity and improving fluency, they occasionally introduce semantic shifts or omit critical health information.

unlisted_practices: Few-shot prompt engineering and ensembling to improve simplification fidelity
RLHF fine-tuning toward user-specific readability targets

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, BioBERT, PubMedGPT) on simplifying health literacy materials using automated metrics and expert annotations; focuses on model capabilities and basic prompt/RLHF strategies rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
